Project OUTPOST
Code-Name: sol3935
(derived from one sol )

OUTPOST is a browser-based Mars survival game that challenges players to manage a three-person crew and keep a Martian outpost operational across a 30-sol (30 martian days) mission.

Players assign crew members to daily jobs, balance power and oxygen supplies, maintain radiation shielding, and respond to emergencies. As each Martian day unfolds, the outpost reacts to player decisions through animated crew activities, changing environmental conditions, resource updates and mission reports.

OUTPOST combines interactive gameplay with educational concepts about Mars exploration. It incorporates historical NASA DONKI space-weather records and NASA/JPL Horizons data to introduce players to solar activity and the communication delays between Earth and Mars.

Designed to make space exploration concepts accessible to younger audiences, OUTPOST turns the challenges of sustaining a Mars habitat into an interactive learning experience.

--> Created by Team HORIZON for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026.
details:
Project Description — OUTPOST (SOL3935)

The Idea

What would it actually take to keep a small crew alive on Mars?

OUTPOST is our attempt to turn that question into an interactive experience. It is a browser-based Mars survival game where players take responsibility for a three-person crew and their outpost over a 30-sol mission.

How It Works

Players take the role of the outpost commander. Each sol, they decide how the crew should spend their time by assigning jobs and managing limited resources.

The main challenges include maintaining sufficient power, ensuring the crew has enough oxygen, building radiation shielding, and keeping the crew healthy. Players also have to respond to emergencies and unexpected environmental conditions.

The game shows the consequences of these decisions through an animated Martian outpost. Crew members move around the base, the environment changes throughout the day, resources are updated, and players receive a report at the end of each sol.

The goal is to make it through all 30 sols while keeping the crew and outpost operational.

Science and NASA Data

OUTPOST uses historical space-weather records from NASA's DONKI database and Earth–Mars light-time data from NASA/JPL Horizons.

These resources help introduce players to real challenges of space exploration, including solar activity and the communication delay between Earth and Mars.

The game also includes simplified models of resource consumption, power generation, radiation shielding, and crew wellbeing. These are designed for gameplay and learning, rather than being exact engineering simulations.

Technology and Development

OUTPOST is built using HTML, CSS and JavaScript, with a modular structure and no requirement for paid APIs or services to play the game.

We use locally stored data so the game can run without needing to retrieve NASA data every time someone plays. The project is published as a static website through GitHub Pages.

Intended Impact

Our aim is to make the challenges of living on Mars easier to understand, especially for younger audiences.

Instead of simply reading about oxygen, radiation, power systems and communication delays, players get to make decisions and see how those decisions affect a mission.

We wanted to create something that is both educational and genuinely enjoyable to play — a small step towards making space exploration more accessible.
